title: Globalisation — core set
titleVi: Toàn cầu hoá — bộ từ cốt lõi
description: Bộ từ về thương mại quốc tế, chuỗi cung ứng và những hệ quả văn hoá của toàn cầu hoá. Nhóm này cho bạn vốn từ để bàn cả mặt lợi và mặt hại thay vì chỉ khen hoặc chỉ chê.
ieltsUse: Dùng cho Task 2 các đề về thương mại tự do, việc làm bị chuyển ra nước ngoài, đồng hoá văn hoá và khoảng cách giàu nghèo giữa các quốc gia.

words.def: the process by which economies and cultures become connected worldwide
words.example: Globalisation has lowered prices for consumers but weakened job security in older industries.

words.vi: liên kết chặt chẽ với nhau
words.def: linked so that changes in one part affect the others
words.example: National economies are now so interconnected that a crisis in one region spreads within days.

words.def: a company operating in several countries
words.example: A multinational corporation can shift production abroad when wages rise at home.

words.def: paying an outside company to perform work previously done internally
words.example: Outsourcing customer service has cut costs but damaged brand loyalty.

words.vi: việc chuyển sản xuất ra nước ngoài
words.def: moving a company's operations to another country
words.example: Offshoring has eliminated thousands of manufacturing jobs in the region.

words.def: the removal of barriers to international trade
words.example: Trade liberalisation lifted millions out of poverty but also exposed small farmers to competition.

words.def: a tax on goods entering or leaving a country
words.example: A tariff on imported steel raises costs for domestic carmakers.

words.def: trade between countries without taxes or restrictions
words.example: Advocates of free trade argue that consumers gain from cheaper imports.

words.vi: đầu tư trực tiếp nước ngoài
words.def: money invested by a foreign company in local production
words.example: Foreign direct investment built the factories that now export electronics worldwide.

words.def: the network of companies that produce and deliver a product
words.example: A single blocked port can disrupt an entire global supply chain.

words.vi: sự đồng nhất hoá văn hoá
words.def: the process by which local cultures become increasingly similar
words.example: Critics warn of cultural homogenisation as the same chains appear in every city.

words.vi: ngôn ngữ chung, ngôn ngữ cầu nối
words.def: a shared language used between speakers of different mother tongues
words.example: English now functions as the lingua franca of science and international business.

words.def: the emigration of skilled workers to richer countries
words.example: Brain drain leaves hospitals in poorer countries chronically short of doctors.

words.vi: khoản tiền chuyển về nước của người di cư
words.def: money sent home by workers abroad
words.example: Remittance flows now exceed foreign aid in several developing economies.

words.def: a country with a lower level of industrialisation and income
words.example: A developing country may lack the infrastructure needed to process its own raw materials.

words.def: the state in which countries or groups rely on each other
words.example: Economic interdependence makes war between trading partners far more costly.

words.def: the policy of restricting imports to protect domestic industry
words.example: Rising protectionism threatens the export-led growth of smaller economies.

words.def: the ability to produce a good at a lower opportunity cost than others
words.example: Each country should specialise where it has a comparative advantage, according to classical theory.

words.def: a raw material or product traded in bulk
words.example: Economies that depend on a single commodity are vulnerable to price swings.

words.def: to sell goods to another country
words.example: The country exports coffee to more than forty markets worldwide.

words.vi: chủ nghĩa đế quốc văn hoá
words.def: the dominance of one culture's values and media over others
words.example: Some argue that Hollywood represents a form of cultural imperialism.

words.vi: thế giới phẳng, làng toàn cầu
words.def: the idea that the world has become closely connected like a small community
words.example: The internet has turned the world into a global village for young learners.

words.def: the removal of government rules from an industry
words.example: Financial deregulation in the 1990s is widely blamed for the later banking crisis.

words.def: a country whose economy is growing rapidly
words.example: An emerging economy can grow quickly yet remain vulnerable to capital flight.

words.vi: mang tính quốc tế, đa văn hoá
words.def: containing people and influences from many countries
words.example: The city has become thoroughly cosmopolitan, with restaurants from every continent.
